content: A comprehensive understanding of MHSA compliance within South Africa's telecommunications sector likely requires access to up-to-date and sector-specific regulatory information that integrates current legal requirements under the Act and telecommunications industry practices. Ultimately, while the regulatory landscape in South Africa appears to be shifting towards more robust frameworks in both the telecommunications and occupational safety domains, the precise application of MHSA in this specific sector remains underexplored or insufficiently documented in the available sources. Recognizing the dual imperatives of high technological adoption and near-universal MHSA compliance is absolutely essential for navigating the competitive dynamics of the South African mining communications market. Operating under the legislative mandate of the Electronic Communications Act and the ICASA Act, the authority is fundamentally responsible for maintaining rigorous compliance standards and overseeing regulatory fee collection across the industry [74] . Historically, the regulatory framework between 2020 and 2024 prioritized spectrum allocation as a primary mechanism to expand broadband access and mobile connectivity, thereby driving broader digital inclusion initiatives across South Africa. Spectrum management remains a central national priority, setting the structural foundation upon which contemporary telecommunications infrastructure and subsequent licensing frameworks are built. Recent regulatory developments reflect a proactive approach to industry oversight and resource management. For instance, ICASA introduced new regulations concerning satellite internet services that became effective on May 18, 2026, demonstrating the authority's active involvement in regulating emerging connectivity solutions [72] . Concurrently, the authority has focused on evolving broadcasting regulations, specifically addressing the reallocation of multiplexes and the enhancement of digital television standards to meet modern broadcasting requirements [56] . Furthermore, ongoing efforts to revise spectrum-related rules are evident in the recent publication of draft amendments to radio frequency spectrum regulations and associated fees, which involved a public consultation deadline of June 29, 2026 [73] .
